evidence.detail: rs/r/J owns a 100,000-particle live map/recycle-id list and preserves the exact diagnostic '[CPU] Reached max capacity of particle pool!' when allocation reaches that bound.

Its allocator accepts the R50 ParticleDefinition plus four spawn/state integers, creates an R50 Particle when no recycled instance exists, or resets and reinitializes a recycled Particle with the new definition/state.
Particle removal decrements the live count and either records the particle id in the reusable-id list or evicts the backing map entry when the recycle pool itself reaches 100,000.
R30 Model calls this allocator directly while emitting model/world particles, fixing the pool as the CPU Particle allocation authority rather than the separate R98 GPU particle pool.

candidates.note: Descriptive semantic recovery from exact-v308 R50 Particle allocation/recycling behavior; original stripped source identifier is not claimed.

evidence.detail: Client allocates one rs/r/K instance for every R50 ParticleDefinition and stores them in its particle-renderer array; each instance owns that definition plus active/removal lists of R50 Particle objects.
The render/update pass ticks each Particle, sends expired particles back to CpuParticlePool, queues them for removal, and removes them from the active list after traversal.

When GPU mode is not active, the class projects each live particle into screen/depth coordinates and alpha-blends its color directly into the Client rs/l/C pixel buffer while checking the scene depth buffer.

When the GPU path is active the class still advances particle lifecycle but skips its software rasterization body, distinguishing this CPU renderer from R98's GpuParticleInstance/Pool/Batch subsystem.

candidates.note: Descriptive semantic recovery from exact-v308 per-definition CPU Particle update/software-render behavior; original stripped source identifier is not claimed.
